title: Why Does Moss Need the Rain? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Every monsoon, soft green velvet covers Diya's compound wall. In summer it turns dry and brown. Why does it need the rain so much? This lesson covers bryophytes, the amphibians of the plant kingdom, from NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 3, Plant Kingdom.

You will see the body of a bryophyte (rhizoids, no true root, stem or leaf) and why the green plant is the haploid gametophyte. A live zoom ladder goes from the wall to a moss cushion, one labelled moss plant and its capsule full of spores. Five animated stages show the antheridium and archegonium, biflagellate antherozoids swimming through water, the zygote, the sporophyte (foot, seta, capsule) growing on the green plant, and spores made by meiosis. We compare liverworts (Marchantia, gemma cups and gemmae) with mosses (protonema and the leafy stage; Funaria, Polytrichum, Sphagnum), then their uses. Then a worked example, the exam trap about the green moss plant, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 23 of our PUC Biology series.
Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.
